headline: Brent $106.48 +1.7% on US Qeshm strike, Apple -4% pre-market, Dec hike odds 73%, midterms today
stance: Brent +1.7% overnight (~5am ET) on a US strike at Qeshm, after Monday's drop on Iran deal talk. Two megacap beats sold off on guidance; the vote lands tonight.

news.head: Apple -4% pre-market on a holiday-quarter margin guide
news.body: Beat: revenue $114.48bn vs $113.39bn, EPS $2.10 vs $1.99. Dec-quarter gross margin guided 45-46% vs 47.9%; services growth 8-9% vs 10.7% expected.

news.head: Palantir -3% after hours despite a beat and raise
news.body: Revenue $2.31bn vs $2.18bn; Q4 guide $2.65bn vs $2.46bn; FY raised to $8.53bn. US commercial revenue passed government for the first time.

news.head: Marvell buys Lumentum for $115bn in stock, both fall
news.body: 4.5 Marvell shares per Lumentum share, a 24% premium to Oct 28. Marvell -12.7% and Lumentum -18.6% Monday; close expected in H1 2028.

news.head: Oracle sells $10bn of bonds at 7-8.65% coupons, stock -8.8%
news.body: Plus $10bn of equity at $116, 11% below Friday. The whole four-year $20bn raise cap, used in one day. S&P cut Meta's outlook to negative on AI capex.

implications: Oil's answer to a US strike was +1.7%, after Monday's drop on deal talk. Deal headlines move it more than strikes do; the Hormuz reopening terms are the trade.
Prediction markets price ~77% odds of a Democratic sweep. The surprise is a Republican hold: higher yields and a stronger dollar at Wednesday's open.

watch.head: JOLTS 10:00
watch.body: Consensus 7.10mn openings vs 7.079mn in August. Factory orders at the same time.

watch.head: Midterms: first polls close 6pm ET
watch.body: Most of the East closes by 8pm. Results arrive overnight, so Wednesday's open prices the outcome.

watch.head: AMD reports after today's close
watch.body: Consensus revenue $13.09bn, EPS $1.95, against a ~$13bn guide. Stock -26% in a month, +1.3% pre-market (~4:45am ET).

watch.head: Refunding Nov 4, 8:30; ISM Services 10:00
watch.body: Coupon-size guidance for the long end is the event. BoE Thursday, jobs report Nov 6.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: US struck Qeshm Island in Hormuz late Monday; Brent $106.48, +1.7% (~5am ET). Trump: a deal "could happen". Iran offers to reopen Hormuz on conditions.
Dec hike odds 73%, from 80% a week ago. 10y 4.92%, 2y 4.60% (~5am ET), 1-2bp higher overnight. The December hike is priced off Hormuz.
ISM 55.5 Monday, +1 vs September against a flat consensus. RBA hiked 25bp to 4.85% Tuesday, 6-3, no December signal; AUD/USD below 0.70.
sections.positioning: Specs extended short Euro, 1st %ile, and sterling, 5th %ile, 6 weeks running: background, not news. Nothing new in rates COT this week.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: Nasdaq 100 closed in a correction Monday; SOX -3.4%. Dow finished higher: the selling is in chips, not the index.
S&P futures -0.2%, Nasdaq 100 futures flat, Dow futures -0.5% (~4am ET). Stoxx 600 -0.6%, Kospi -3.6%, Taiwan -3.6%, steepest since late July.
Monday's megacap beats fell after hours on guidance. Beats are not enough; outlooks are what trade this week.
sections.positioning: Specs extended short VIX, 13th %ile, and extended long Russell 2000, 99th, 4-5 weeks running: background. The vote lands on both tonight.

single_name.note: New to the setups list Monday: insider buy filed Oct 29, trading above its 200-day, 3.3 days to cover. Score 5, top of the list.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: 17 IG issuers priced Monday, the most since Sep 8. Dealers see ~$45bn this week, front-loaded before the vote and payrolls.
Tech IG spreads 108bp Friday vs 76bp at end-2025: AI capex is now a credit story. A $10bn AI bond deal priced at 7-8.65% Monday.
BDCs 0.90x NAV at Monday's close, up from 0.89x Friday, with equities down: the private-credit discount is not tracking tech.
